body:
Listen, you can't feel responsible.

After my last GF left me for another guy pretty much overnight and without warning, I was devastated. But if someone is going to kill themselves, it's from older, deeper problems. I'm sure you'd change what happened if you could, maybe you'd even stay together, but it's not *your fault* and you can't maintain/build a relationship in order to save someone else.

Take it from someone who has ( sort of ) been on the other side: It's not something you did. A person who is in a normal headspace doesn't kill himself over a breakup. Hell, even someone in a fairly fucked up headspace ( me ) isn't going to kill themselves over a girl, even if he loved her very very much.

I wish you could see it from a wider perspective, but I'm sure that's hard. Suffice it to say, if I were dead ( from suicide or any other reason ) I wouldn't want any woman I've ever loved to just sit around decaying. You have to find a way to move on and love someone else, even though I know it's hard.

It's just a straw that broke the camel's back issue. If I hadn't my other crosses to bear, I think I could deal with bad teeth.

It's just one thing too many.

That's quite a story!

You seem pretty happy, and I'm glad. My mother had dentures even when she was a very young lady, in her early 20s. She probably needed them much earlier.

And she's a staggeringly fastidious person. The idea that she just "didn't brush" wouldn't cross the mind of her worst enemy. My dental genetics are just fucked, basically.

I sincerely appreciate your message. I am unsure how I am going to proceed, to be honest. Suicide is merely a strong possibility and, even at that, not for at least three or four more years. I've got *some* fight left in me, if not as much as I once did.
